problem.claim: Discover unknown treatment effects directly from trial data, using representations of unstructured trial data interpreted through a Sparse Auto Encoder.

gap.claim: Hand-crafted hypotheses, expensive analysis, multiple-testing issues, and entangled effects limit causal-effect estimation at scale and may anchor discovery on incomplete hypotheses.

contributions.claim: Introduces Neural Effect Search, a recursive procedure based on progressive stratification to address multiple testing and effect entanglement.
Combines pretrained foundation-model representations of unstructured trial data with Sparse Auto Encoder interpretation for exploratory causal inference.
Applies the approach to experimental ecology and reports unsupervised causal-effect identification on a real-world scientific trial.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe Neural Effect Search as a novel procedure and the real-world demonstration as the first successful unsupervised causal-effect identification in a scientific trial.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report assessing algorithm robustness on semi-synthetic experiments.
The authors report successful unsupervised causal-effect identification on a real-world experimental-ecology trial.

narrative_sequence.summary: RCT-based science depends on hand-crafted hypotheses and costly analysis, constraining causal discovery at scale.
The proposal converts unstructured trial data into foundation-model representations and interprets them with a Sparse Auto Encoder.
Neural-level effect discovery is complicated by multiple testing and entangled effects.
Neural Effect Search uses progressive stratification; the authors report semi-synthetic robustness assessment and a real-world ecology-trial demonstration.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly links the representation pipeline to two named statistical or structural obstacles and presents progressive stratification as the mechanism addressing both.

lessons.interpretation: A compact abstract can make a method’s rationale auditable by pairing each technical component with a specific challenge.
lessons.application: When presenting a new discovery pipeline, map each major component to an explicitly named failure mode and state the mechanism intended to address it.
lessons.exception: Avoid this framing when the component-to-challenge mapping is speculative or unsupported by the reported method.

unknowns: The abstract gives no semi-synthetic datasets, metrics, robustness criteria, sample sizes, or quantitative results.
The identified effects, trial details, comparison methods, and conditions for the real-world demonstration are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independently verified correctness, reproducibility, or priority of the stated novelty.
